questions.prompt: Explain what a result builder is in Swift, why SE-0289 standardized it in Swift 5.4, and what problems it solves for declarative APIs.
questions.modelAnswer: A result builder is a Swift type marked with @resultBuilder that translates sequential closure statements into static builder method calls. SE-0289 standardized result builders in Swift 5.4 after their initial introduction in SwiftUI. Before result builders, constructing hierarchies required comma-separated arrays or repetitive append calls. Result builders eliminate syntactic noise by turning lines of code into structured composite values. This enables clean declarative APIs like SwiftUI views and regex builders with full compile-time type safety.

rubric.criterion: Defines result builders as compiler-driven closure transformations via @resultBuilder
Identifies SE-0289 standardization in Swift 5.4
Contrasts with verbose arrays, commas, and manual append calls
Highlights declarative syntax and static type safety in DSLs like SwiftUI

questions.prompt: Explain the roles of buildBlock, buildOptional, and buildEither in a result builder. Why are all three needed for complete control flow support?
questions.modelAnswer: buildBlock is the required core method that merges sequential statements into one combined component. buildOptional handles conditional statements lacking an else branch by taking an optional component. buildEither provides first: and second: variants to handle binary selection in if-else and multi-case switch statements. Without buildOptional and buildEither, attempting to write if or switch constructs inside a builder closure triggers compiler errors. Together, these three methods allow standard Swift control flow within declarative builder closures.

rubric.criterion: Explains buildBlock as the core sequential combiner
Explains buildOptional for single if conditions with optional components
Explains buildEither(first:) and buildEither(second:) for if-else and switch branching
Explains compile-time errors that occur when control flow methods are missing

questions.prompt: Explain buildExpression and buildFinalResult in a result builder. How do they enable input transformation and customized return types?
questions.modelAnswer: buildExpression intercepts each individual expression before it reaches buildBlock. It can overload different parameter types to convert varied inputs into a single internal component type. buildFinalResult executes after all components have been gathered by buildBlock. It transforms the final accumulated component into the ultimate return type exposed to callers. Together, they decouple the input types and final output type from the internal component type used during block building.

rubric.criterion: Explains buildExpression intercepts individual statements to normalize input types
Explains buildFinalResult converts accumulated components into the final return type
Explains decoupling of input syntax, internal components, and final output type

questions.prompt: Explain how SwiftUI uses @ViewBuilder to construct view hierarchies. How does it handle multiple child views, and why does TupleView exist?
questions.modelAnswer: SwiftUI annotates the body property and container closures with @ViewBuilder. When you list views on separate lines, @ViewBuilder groups them into strongly typed TupleView structures. For instance, two views produce TupleView<(ViewA, ViewB)>. In earlier Swift versions, buildBlock overloaded up to ten view parameters. Swift now uses parameter packs and variadic generics to support arbitrary view counts. TupleView preserves exact static type hierarchies without type erasure overhead.

rubric.criterion: Explains @ViewBuilder role in view body and container closures
Identifies TupleView as the static composite representation of child views
Discusses 10-view limit history and modern variadic generics / parameter packs
Highlights static type preservation and avoiding type erasure

questions.prompt: Contrast result builders with Swift macros. When would you use a result builder, and when would you use a macro?
questions.modelAnswer: Result builders and Swift macros serve different metaprogramming roles. Result builders transform closure statements into method chains to build embedded domain-specific languages at compile time. They cannot create new properties or inspect types. Swift macros operate directly on abstract syntax trees to synthesize arbitrary code anywhere, such as adding member properties or conforming types. You use result builders for declarative content construction like SwiftUI views. You use macros for code generation and boilerplate elimination across types.

rubric.criterion: Distinguishes closure method call transformation from AST syntax generation
Identifies result builder scope: closures and declarative DSL construction
Identifies macro scope: arbitrary code synthesis, member additions, and conformances
Provides clear selection criteria and practical use cases for each tool
